# Rentzu Manual Testing (Android emulator) — BASE SKILL

This is the **foundation skill** for all Rentzu app testing. It gets the backend, emulator, and
Expo app running (or verifies they already are), logs in, and leaves everything in a known,
running, authenticated state. Other test skills (e.g. "add a property", "record an expense",
"switch organizations") are expected to **depend on this skill** rather than re-implement any of
its setup or login logic — see **§7 Contract for downstream skills**.

Repo root in this environment: `D:\apps\rentzu`. Helper script:
`D:\apps\rentzu\.agents\skills\rentzu-manual-testing\scripts\ui-helpers.ps1`.

## 0.1. HARD RULE — a tap/type/Enter with no observable reaction is never "retry and move on"

If a scripted tap, `Type-IntoFocusedField`/`Set-RentzuFieldValue` call, or an Enter/submit action
does **not** produce the expected UI change (no navigation, no field text, no toast, no new
element in the next dump) — **stop and diagnose before continuing the test flow.** Do not just
retry the same call, guess new coordinates, or route around it silently. This matters because a
silent no-op (as opposed to a thrown error) is exactly how prior pitfalls #9/#10/#12 in this file
were discovered — the symptom is quiet, so it's easy to paper over instead of fix.

Required steps when this happens:

1. **Re-dump and inspect.** Call `Get-UiDump` fresh and check: did the element you tapped actually
   exist at those bounds? Is a system dialog, keyboard toolbar, or overlay (Metro/LogBox, ANR,
   Gboard toolbar) sitting on top of the target? Is the field's `focused` attribute what you
   expected before/after?
2. **Take a screenshot** (`Take-Screenshot`) to visually confirm what's actually on screen when the
   dump alone doesn't make it obvious.
3. **Identify the root cause** — stale bounds from a layout shift, a race with Metro
   bundling/HMR, a missing re-dump after a transition, wrong anchor text/content-desc, an
   overlay intercepting the tap, etc. Don't accept "it just didn't work" as the final answer.
4. **Fix `ui-helpers.ps1` and/or this SKILL.md** once the cause is known, so the same failure
   doesn't have to be rediscovered next session:
   - If it's a reusable timing/overlay/focus problem, encode the fix in a helper function (follow
     the pattern of `Dismiss-RentzuMetroOverlay`, `Confirm-RentzuLoggedIn`'s poll loop, or
     `Set-RentzuFieldValue`'s verify-before-type check).
   - Document the failure mode as a new numbered entry under "Known pitfalls" below, including
     what the false signal looked like and what the fix was.
   - Use the standard AI attribution comments (`<!-- Modified by AI on MM/DD/YYYY. Edit #N. ... -->`
     at the top of this file, `# Modified by AI on MM/DD/YYYY. Edit #N.` above the changed function
     in `ui-helpers.ps1`) and bump the version in the frontmatter if the change is substantive.
5. Only after the fix is in place, retry the original test step using the corrected helper/flow.

This rule applies to this skill and to every downstream skill that drives the UI — if a downstream
skill's script hits this situation, fix it here (the shared helper file) rather than working around
it locally in the downstream skill.

## 0. Read this first — session conflicts and stale processes

The backend, the emulator, and the Expo dev server are **long-running processes that can already
be running** from an earlier turn of this conversation, or (less often) left over as orphaned OS
processes from a previous, unrelated session. Blindly re-running the three startup commands every
time causes port conflicts (8000, 8081) and duplicate/wedged emulator instances. Always check
before you act:

1. Call the CLI's own `list_powershell` tool and look for existing shellIds whose command matches
   `run-server.cmd`, `run-app.cmd`, or `emulator.exe`. If one is `status: running`, don't start a
   second one blindly — health-check it first (see step 2) and reuse it if healthy.
2. Dot-source `ui-helpers.ps1` (see §2) and call `Get-RentzuSessionStatus`. This is the
   **authoritative, OS-level** check (TCP listeners on 8000/8081, `adb devices`) — it doesn't rely
   on the CLI's shell bookkeeping, so it also catches processes orphaned from a previous CLI
   session. It reports, per component, whether the port is bound and whether it's actually healthy
   (answers the expected HTTP response).
3. Decide from that status:
   - **Healthy → reuse it.** Don't restart. Restarting a booted emulator alone can cost minutes.
   - **Port bound but unhealthy** (stale/crashed process) → call `Ensure-RentzuBackendClean` /
     `Ensure-RentzuExpoClean` to kill just that port's owning process, then start the component
     fresh per §1/§3.
   - **Emulator shows `offline` in `adb devices`** (wedged) → call `Ensure-RentzuEmulatorClean`,
     then boot fresh per §2 below.
   - **Nothing running** → start fresh per §1–§4.

`run-server.cmd` already does its own port-8000 + stale-uvicorn cleanup internally (see its
source), so it's usually safe to just re-run — the helper functions exist mainly for Expo/Metro
(which has no such self-cleanup) and for the emulator.

## 1. Start (or reuse) the backend

```pwsh
cd D:\apps\rentzu
.\run-server.cmd
```

Wait for `Uvicorn running on http://0.0.0.0:8000`. Verify:
`curl.exe -s http://127.0.0.1:8000/` → `{"ok":true,"service":"rentzu-api"}`.

Requires PostgreSQL running locally (`DATABASE_URL` in `.env`) — check with
`Get-Service -Name postgresql*`. Verification codes are random per request and
delivered by SMTP; the old `RENTZU_FIXED_VERIFICATION_CODE=123456` bypass has
been **removed**. Tests read the live code from Postgres via
`Get-RentzuVerificationCode` (see §6), so no real inbox is needed — but SMTP
must be configured in `.env` or `/auth/request-code` returns 503.

## 2. Start (or reuse) the Android emulator

```pwsh
& "D:\andriodsdk\emulator\emulator.exe" -list-avds     # this env has "Pixel_8"
& "D:\andriodsdk\emulator\emulator.exe" -avd Pixel_8
```

Poll with `adb devices` / `adb shell getprop sys.boot_completed` (returns `1` when ready), or use
the helper `Wait-ForEmulatorBoot` (in `ui-helpers.ps1`). Expo Go (`host.exp.exponent`) is
pre-installed on this AVD image — confirm with `adb shell pm list packages | Select-String expo`.

## 3. Start (or reuse) the Expo dev server

```pwsh
cd D:\apps\rentzu
.\run-app.cmd
```

Wait for `Waiting on http://localhost:8081`. Verify:
`curl.exe -s http://127.0.0.1:8081/status` → `packager-status:running`.

`app/src/services/api.ts` points at `http://10.0.2.2:8000` (the Android emulator's alias for the
host's `localhost`), so no config changes are needed for the emulator to reach the local backend.

## Visibility requirement — never hide these three processes' logs

`run-server.cmd`, `run-app.cmd`, and `emulator.exe` must **always** be launched as the sole command
of their own top-level `powershell` tool call (e.g. shellIds named `backend`, `expo`, `emulator`),
**never** from inside a dot-sourced script, `Start-Process`, `Start-Job`, or any other wrapped/
backgrounded/hidden subprocess. If they're started that way, their stdout/stderr (uvicorn request
logs, Metro bundling progress, emulator boot diagnostics) becomes invisible to the user — which is
the whole reason this note exists: it was called out explicitly because it happened once. The
helper script `ui-helpers.ps1` **intentionally contains no function that launches any of these
three** — only read-only status checks and UI-driving helpers. Keep it that way. The user can read
these logs at any time via the CLI's `read_powershell` on the corresponding shellId.

## 4. Open the app in Expo Go on the emulator

```pwsh
adb shell am start -a android.intent.action.VIEW -d "exp://10.0.2.2:8081"
```

Use the emulator's host alias `10.0.2.2`, not `127.0.0.1` (which is the emulator itself). Watch the
Expo terminal for `Android Bundled <ms> ... AppEntry.js (N modules)` to confirm the bundle loaded.

## 5. Driving the UI reliably — use `ui-helpers.ps1`, don't eyeball screenshots

Screenshots downscale for display, so tapping coordinates read off a rendered image is unreliable
and wastes turns. `ui-helpers.ps1` wraps the reliable pattern (dump UI hierarchy → read exact
`bounds="[x1,y1][x2,y2]"` → tap the center) in reusable functions:

```pwsh
. D:\apps\rentzu\.agents\skills\rentzu-manual-testing\scripts\ui-helpers.ps1

Get-UiDump                                        # refresh the cached hierarchy dump
Get-ElementBounds -Text "Sign Out"                # or -ContentDesc "Account"
Tap-ElementByText "Continue with email"           # dump + find + tap + settle, one call
Tap-ElementByContentDesc "Account"
Type-IntoFocusedField "vampirel1988@gmail.com"    # call right after the tap that focused the field
Dismiss-Keyboard
Take-Screenshot -Name "after-login"               # returns a local PNG path for the `view` tool
```

Key rules baked into the helpers (know these even if you call the raw functions instead of the
convenience wrappers):

- **Re-dump after every layout change.** Opening/closing the keyboard shrinks the visible content
  area and shifts every button below it — a bounds rectangle from before the keyboard opened is
  stale. `Tap-ElementByText`/`Tap-ElementByContentDesc` always re-dump first, so prefer those.
- **Tap, then type, in the same breath.** Don't batch a tap and a type call across a screen
  transition — `Type-IntoFocusedField` types into whatever currently has focus, so if focus was
  lost (e.g. the tap that was supposed to focus the field actually missed and hit something else)
  the text silently goes nowhere. Screenshot after any `Type-IntoFocusedField` if unsure.
- **Get the real screen resolution once** with `adb shell wm size` if you ever need to reason about
  bounds manually — displayed screenshots are downscaled, real device coordinates are not.
- **`Get-ElementBounds` throws if not found** — treat that as signal to screenshot and inspect,
  not something to catch-and-guess-coordinates around.

## 6. Login flow (email + 6-digit code)

Test account: `vampirel1988@gmail.com` / password `password123`. The verification
code is **random per login** and sent by email, so it can no longer be hardcoded.
`Invoke-RentzuLogin` fetches it automatically with `Get-RentzuVerificationCode`,
which reads the newest `pending` row from the `email_verification_codes` table.
That requires local Postgres access and is deliberately not an API endpoint — the
old fixed-code and `debug_code` bypasses let anyone reaching the API log into any
account, so they were removed.

The password now genuinely authenticates: `/auth/request-code` returns **401** on a
wrong password instead of silently overwriting the account's password hash. Typing
"any password" no longer works — it must be `password123` for this account.

**Prefer calling `Invoke-RentzuLogin` (or better, `Resume-RentzuSession` — see §7) over
reimplementing these taps.** It is idempotent: if the app is already authenticated it returns
immediately without signing out, so it's safe to call at the start of every downstream test. The
manual steps it encodes, for reference / debugging:

1. If a stale/expired session is showing, **Account** tab → **Sign Out** to reach the login screen.
2. Tap **Email**, type the email. Tap **Password**, type `password123` — a wrong
   password is now rejected with 401 before any code is sent.
3. Tap **Continue with email** → navigates to **Verify your email**.
4. Get the code with `Get-RentzuVerificationCode -Email vampirel1988@gmail.com`
   (only valid *after* step 3, since the row is created by `/auth/request-code`).
   Tap the **Verification code** field (placeholder text is literally `123456`),
   type that code, tap **Verify email**.
5. On success, the app lands on the tab navigator (Summary/Property/Tax Ready/Account) with the
   account's real data loaded — no "Token has expired" banner.

Codes are single-use and expire after 10 minutes; requesting a new one supersedes
any earlier pending code. Re-submitting an already-accepted code returns 400, so
always re-fetch after a fresh **Continue with email**.

**Troubleshooting "Invalid verification code":** almost always means the code field never actually
received the typed text — a tap landed on the wrong element after a keyboard-driven layout shift.
Re-dump, confirm `focused="true"` on the target `EditText` node, and retry the tap+type sequence
before resubmitting.

## 7. Contract for downstream skills — how to depend on this one

Any skill that tests a feature past the login screen (adding a property, recording an expense,
switching organizations, billing, language, etc.) should treat this skill as its required
precondition, and follow this contract so tests chain together instead of stepping on each other:

1. **Re-source `ui-helpers.ps1` at the top of every `powershell` tool call that needs it.** Each
   `powershell` tool invocation is a **fresh process** — dot-sourced functions and variables from
   an earlier call do **not** persist. This is not optional boilerplate; forgetting it is the most
   common way a downstream skill's script fails with "term not recognized" errors:
   ```pwsh
   . D:\apps\rentzu\.agents\skills\rentzu-manual-testing\scripts\ui-helpers.ps1
   # ... your commands using its functions, in the SAME powershell call ...
   ```
2. **Call `Resume-RentzuSession` first, every time**, instead of assuming the environment from a
   previous skill invocation is still exactly as you left it:
   ```pwsh
   $status = Resume-RentzuSession
   if (-not $status.Ready)    { throw "Backend/Expo/emulator not healthy: $($status | ConvertTo-Json)" }
   if (-not $status.LoggedIn) { throw "Login did not succeed: $($status | ConvertTo-Json)" }
   # continue this skill's own test steps here — the app is authenticated and on Summary.
   ```
   `Resume-RentzuSession` is safe to call any number of times, from any skill, in any order: it
   never signs out an already-authenticated session, never restarts a healthy backend/Expo/
   emulator, and only repairs what's actually broken. This is what lets test skill B continue
   exactly where test skill A left off (mid-portfolio, same org selected, etc.) instead of forcing
   a fresh login that would reset in-app navigation state.
3. **Never tear down the backend, Expo, or emulator shells when your skill finishes.** Leave them
   running so the next skill in the chain (or the user) can keep using them. Only stop a component
   if the user explicitly asks to shut everything down, or `Resume-RentzuSession` told you it was
   unhealthy and needed a clean restart.
4. **If your skill needs to test the logout/login cycle itself**, call
   `Invoke-RentzuLogin -ForceReLogin` explicitly rather than signing out via raw taps — it's the
   one documented way to intentionally bypass the idempotent reuse check.
5. **Use `Confirm-RentzuLoggedIn`** (read-only, never throws) for a quick yes/no check without the
   side effect of potentially logging in — e.g. to assert a test that logs out actually left the
   app on the login screen.

## 8. Smoke-test reference — main tabs

Bottom tab bar items are `content-desc`: `Summary`, `Property`, `Tax Ready`, `👤, Account`.

- **Summary**: org switcher, net year-to-date, income/expenses, properties list with per-property
  record counts and a voice-record mic button.
- **Property** (tap a property card, or the Property tab for the last-viewed one): Overview /
  Records / Documents sub-tabs, net cash flow chart, income/expenses, "Quick record" shortcuts
  (Rent / Expense / Improvement) and a voice mic FAB.
- **Tax Ready**: org + tax-year pickers, "All Properties Summary" vs per-property tabs, estimated
  tax impact, deduction summary breakdown (Rent, Legal & Professional, Management, Maintenance &
  Repairs, Other Expenses, Additional Income), totals.
- **Account**: email, Organizations (Create organization), Plan/billing (Free vs Free trial +
  Start subscription), Language (English/中文), Sign Out.

Verified against the `vampirel1988@gmail.com` test account in this environment: org "Jason Liang",
2 properties (`33 Selye` – Single Family, 1 unit, 11 records; `44 Hawkins` – Duplex, 2 units, 9
records), net YTD -$7,786.54 (income $4,400.00 / expenses $12,186.54).

## Reference: helper script functions (`scripts/ui-helpers.ps1`)

| Function | Purpose |
|---|---|
| `Get-RentzuSessionStatus` | OS-level snapshot: backend/Expo port bound + healthy, emulator serial. Call first. |
| `Test-RentzuBackendHealthy` / `Test-RentzuExpoHealthy` | HTTP health checks for ports 8000/8081. |
| `Get-RunningEmulatorSerial` | Returns a booted emulator's serial, or `$null`. |
| `Stop-ProcessOnPort` | Kills only the process bound to a given port. |
| `Ensure-RentzuBackendClean` / `Ensure-RentzuExpoClean` | Clean a port only if bound-but-unhealthy. |
| `Ensure-RentzuEmulatorClean` | Kills a wedged/offline emulator so a fresh one can boot. |
| `Get-UiDump` | Pulls a fresh `uiautomator` XML dump. |
| `Get-ElementBounds` | Finds a node by exact `text` or `content-desc`, returns center coords. |
| `Tap-Bounds` / `Tap-ElementByText` / `Tap-ElementByContentDesc` | Tap helpers (the latter two dump-first). |
| `Type-IntoFocusedField` | Types into the currently-focused `EditText`. |
| `Set-RentzuFieldValue` | **Use this for every login/signup field** — clears + types + verifies, safe against stale-focus/toolbar bugs (see "Known pitfalls" #8-10). |
| `Dismiss-Keyboard` | Closes the soft keyboard (and any Gboard floating toolbar) via KEYCODE_ESCAPE — never use the hardware back button for this. |
| `Dismiss-RentzuMetroOverlay` | Dismisses the cosmetic "Cannot connect to Metro" HMR toast/LogBox (see "Known pitfalls" #12) — `Confirm-RentzuLoggedIn` calls this automatically inside its poll loop. |
| `Take-Screenshot` | Pulls a PNG for visual inspection with the `view` tool. |
| `Wait-ForEmulatorBoot` | Polls `sys.boot_completed` until ready or timeout. |
| `Confirm-RentzuLoggedIn` | Read-only: is the app currently on the authenticated tab navigator? |
| `Invoke-RentzuLogin` | Idempotent login; `-ForceReLogin` to bypass reuse. |
| `Resume-RentzuSession` | **Single entry point for downstream skills** — see §7. |
| `Read-XmlDump` | Reads a `uiautomator` dump as `[xml]` with forced UTF-8 decoding — see "Known pitfalls" below. |

## Known pitfalls already fixed in `ui-helpers.ps1` (do not reintroduce)

These three bugs were found and fixed while building/validating this skill. If you're editing
`ui-helpers.ps1`, know about them so you don't undo the fix:

1. **`$pid` is read-only in PowerShell.** It's the automatic variable holding the *current*
   process ID. Using it as a loop variable (`foreach ($pid in ...)`) throws `VariableNotWritable`.
   `Stop-ProcessOnPort` uses `$procId` instead — never rename it back to `$pid`.
2. **`Invoke-WebRequest`'s `.Content` can silently return a raw `byte[]` instead of decoded text**
   on this PowerShell install, for plain-text endpoints like `/status` and `/` (likely missing/
   unexpected `Content-Type`). A `-match` against a byte array is always falsy, so a health check
   built on `Invoke-WebRequest` reports "unhealthy" even when the server is demonstrably fine —
   this actually caused `Ensure-RentzuExpoClean` to kill a healthy, already-running Expo dev
   server (twice, during development of this skill). **Fix**: `Test-RentzuBackendHealthy` and
   `Test-RentzuExpoHealthy` shell out to `curl.exe` instead, which returns decoded text directly.
   Never change these two functions back to `Invoke-WebRequest` without re-verifying against a
   live `curl.exe` check first.
3. **`Get-Content -Raw` misdecodes the UTF-8 `uiautomator` XML dump**, using the system codepage
   instead of UTF-8. The app's `content-desc` values sometimes contain emoji (multi-byte UTF-8).
   Misdecoding those bytes can swallow an adjacent ASCII `"` character, corrupting the XML
   attribute quoting and making `[xml]$xml = ...` throw `InvalidCastToXmlDocument` ("false" is an
   unexpected token...). **Fix**: always read dumps through `Read-XmlDump` (uses
   `[System.IO.File]::ReadAllText($Path, [System.Text.Encoding]::UTF8)`), never `Get-Content -Raw`
   directly, when parsing a dump as `[xml]`.
4. **`Confirm-RentzuLoggedIn` needs to retry, not dump once.** Right after opening the app (fresh
   `adb shell am start` deep link) or right after Metro finishes a rebuild, there's a real window —
   often several seconds — where the app is on a splash/loading screen showing neither the
   authenticated tabs nor the login form. A single immediate dump can land in that window and
   falsely report "not logged in", which then sends `Invoke-RentzuLogin` down the login-form path
   even though the app is already authenticated underneath (observed in practice: a persisted JWT
   survived a full backend/Expo/emulator restart because Expo Go's storage lives on the emulator
   disk, not the dev server). **Fix**: `Confirm-RentzuLoggedIn` polls for up to `-TimeoutSec`
   (default 20s), re-dumping every `-PollIntervalSec`, and only returns once it sees either the
   authenticated tabs or a recognizable login/verify-screen marker.
5. **The bottom tab bar's `content-desc` is not reliable for the Account tab — use `text=`
   instead.** Summary/Property/Tax Ready tabs have `content-desc="Summary"` etc. (matches their
   `text=` exactly), but the Account tab's `content-desc` is `"👤, Account"` (an emoji + ", Account"
   — presumably an accessibility label), not `"Account"`. An exact-match lookup via
   `Get-ElementBounds -ContentDesc "Account"` / `Tap-ElementByContentDesc "Account"` always misses.
   Each tab also has a separate `text="Account"` node (the label under the icon), which matches
   exactly. **Fix**: always navigate tabs with `Tap-ElementByText`, never
   `Tap-ElementByContentDesc`, even though `content-desc` happens to work for the other three tabs
   — consistency avoids re-discovering this the hard way per-tab.
6. **`Invoke-RentzuLogin`'s sign-out check must navigate to the Account tab first.** The "Sign
   Out" button only exists as a node when the Account tab is showing — checking for it in whatever
   dump happens to be cached (e.g. still on Summary from a resumed session) always finds nothing,
   silently skips the sign-out tap, and falls through to the email-field lookup, which then throws
   because the app is still showing the authenticated Summary screen. **Fix**: only when
   `Confirm-RentzuLoggedIn` has confirmed the app is authenticated does `Invoke-RentzuLogin`
   navigate to the Account tab (`Tap-ElementByText "Account"`) before checking for/tapping
   "Sign Out". (A logged-out app has no tabs to navigate to at all, so this is skipped when not
   authenticated — including when `-ForceReLogin` is passed but the app happens to already be
   logged out.)
7. **Watch for Android "System UI isn't responding" (ANR) dialogs on a freshly-booted or
   under-load emulator** — they can appear mid-flow (e.g. while Metro is doing its first bundle
   rebuild) and, if a scripted tap lands on the dialog instead of the app underneath (its "Close
   app" button in particular), will kill the app back to the home screen. There is no automatic
   detection/dismissal for this yet — if a flow behaves unexpectedly (e.g. `Confirm-RentzuLoggedIn`
   times out with no definitive signal, or a later step can't find an expected element), always
   `Take-Screenshot` and manually check for a system dialog before assuming the app itself is
   broken. Prefer waiting for Metro's first bundle to fully settle (10-15s after "New update
   available, downloading..." disappears) before driving the UI on a cold-started app.
8. **NEVER dismiss anything with the hardware back button (`adb shell input keyevent 4`).** On
   the app's root screen (no back-stack yet — e.g. the login form), back navigation exits the app
   entirely to the Android home screen instead of closing whatever you meant to dismiss (observed
   in practice while trying to close a stuck Gboard toolbar — see #9). If you need to collapse the
   keyboard or a keyboard-attached overlay, use `Dismiss-Keyboard` (`adb shell input keyevent 111`,
   KEYCODE_ESCAPE) — never keyevent 4.
9. **A Gboard floating "quick access" toolbar (mic / backspace-x / checkmark / emoji / hamburger
   icons pinned to the left edge) can appear after a burst of backspaces, and it is a system-level
   overlay tied to the `InputMethod` window** (confirmed via `adb shell dumpsys window windows`) —
   not part of the RN app, so it **persists across app restarts** and a plain tap on "empty" app
   space does not reliably dismiss it. The only dismissal confirmed to work is `Dismiss-Keyboard`
   (KEYCODE_ESCAPE), which collapses the keyboard and the toolbar together.
10. **Typing into a second field can silently land in the first field instead of throwing.** After
    the keyboard opens/closes or the screen transitions, cached bounds go stale; tapping a *second*
    field (e.g. password) with stale/mistimed bounds can miss and leave focus on the field that was
    already focused, so the new value gets appended there instead — producing a garbled
    concatenation with no error (observed: `"vampirel1988@gmail.compassword123"` all landed in the
    email field, password left empty, login rejected with "Please enter a valid email and
    password."). **Fix (#9 and #10 together)**: use `Set-RentzuFieldValue -AnchorText <placeholder>
    -Value <value>` for every login/signup field instead of a bare `Tap-Bounds` +
    `Type-IntoFocusedField`. It re-dumps before every tap, verifies `focused='true'` actually
    changed before typing, clears via move-end + backspace + `Dismiss-Keyboard` (never back), and
    warns (without throwing) if the resulting field text doesn't match what was typed. Never revert
    `Invoke-RentzuLogin`'s email/password/code entry back to bare taps.
11. **`Set-RentzuFieldValue -AnchorText <placeholder>` can throw "Element not found" if the field
    already has real content.** It locates the field by matching the placeholder's exact `text=`,
    which only exists while the field is empty/showing its placeholder — once real text (or masked
    password dots) has been typed into it, that placeholder node disappears from the dump, so a
    second call with the same `-AnchorText` (e.g. re-running a step after a partial failure, or
    resuming a half-completed form) fails to find it even though the field is already correctly
    filled. **This is expected, not a bug to "fix" by retrying** — before calling
    `Set-RentzuFieldValue` on a form you didn't just render from scratch, take a screenshot first
    and check whether the field already shows the value you wanted; if so, skip that field and move
    on (e.g. proceed straight to `Dismiss-Keyboard` + tapping "Continue with email"). Only call
    `Set-RentzuFieldValue` on fields that are genuinely empty (showing their placeholder).
12. **"Cannot connect to Metro" (small toast or full-screen LogBox) is cosmetic HMR/Fast-Refresh
    WebSocket noise, not a real backend/Expo outage** — it can appear even while
    `Get-RentzuSessionStatus` reports both ports healthy, especially after a burst of adb
    screenshot/input calls (the emulator's virtual network is what's flaky, not Metro or the
    backend). It comes in two forms and they dismiss differently: the small toast banner closes
    with plain `Dismiss-Keyboard` (KEYCODE_ESCAPE), but the **full-screen LogBox does NOT** — ESCAPE
    is swallowed by it, and it must be closed by tapping its actual "Dismiss" button. Left up, the
    full-screen form covers every tab/login marker `Confirm-RentzuLoggedIn` looks for, producing a
    false "no definitive signal... Defaulting to `$false`" even though the app is genuinely fine
    underneath. **Fix**: use `Dismiss-RentzuMetroOverlay` (checks for either form and closes it
    correctly) instead of assuming ESCAPE always works; `Confirm-RentzuLoggedIn`'s poll loop now
    calls it automatically whenever it detects the LogBox mid-poll, so this self-heals in most
    cases, but call it explicitly first if a screenshot shows either form before doing anything
    else on that screen.
13. **The Gboard floating "quick access" toolbar (pitfall #9) is a separate system `InputMethod`
    window, not part of the app, so it's invisible to `Get-UiDump`/uiautomator and can't be
    detected or asserted against there** — confirmed via `adb shell dumpsys window windows`
    (`Window{... InputMethod}: package=com.google.android.inputmethod.latin`). It opens as soon as
    *any* `EditText` is focused (not only after a burst of backspaces, as originally documented for
    pitfall #9), and it is pinned to the **left edge** of the screen, so it can silently intercept a
    subsequent tap that lands there — or a tap using bounds captured before it (or the keyboard)
    finished closing. Found while filling in the "New Property" form: typing the property name
    worked fine, but the very next tap (selecting the "Fourplex" property-type chip) silently did
    nothing — no error, chip just stayed on "Single family" — because the keyboard/toolbar was still
    open/animating shut from the previous field. This is exactly the class of silent no-op §0.1
    requires diagnosing rather than retrying blindly. **Fix**: `Set-RentzuFieldValue` now always
    calls `Dismiss-Keyboard` once more after typing and verifying, right before returning, so the
    keyboard and its toolbar are guaranteed closed before the caller's next tap — never leave a
    field call without closing the keyboard first if you write a new field-filling helper.
14. **`Set-RentzuFieldValue` used to clear-then-retap on every call, even though the field is
    always already empty at that point.** The user noticed this directly by watching the emulator:
    each field visibly opened the keyboard/Gboard sidebar, closed it, then opened it again before
    text finally appeared. Root cause: `-AnchorText` is matched against a field's *placeholder*
    text, which (per pitfall #11) is only rendered while the field is genuinely empty — so a
    successful match already guarantees there's nothing to clear. The old code nonetheless did
    `KEYCODE_MOVE_END` + up to 80x `KEYCODE_DEL` + `Dismiss-Keyboard` + a second tap + a second
    focus check before typing, which is a no-op clear that still pays the full cost of opening and
    closing the keyboard/sidebar twice. **Fix**: removed the clear-and-retap block entirely — tap
    once, confirm focus, type, verify. If a field genuinely needs clearing (real, non-placeholder
    content already present), that's a distinct scenario from what this function is for; don't
    reintroduce a blind clear-every-time "just in case" here.
15. **The emulator IME races `adb shell input text` and can DUPLICATE the leading character.**
    Observed directly by the user watching a `-ForceReLogin`: the email was entered as
    `vvampirel1988@gmail.com` (a doubled leading `v`), which — because dev auth authenticates on the
    6-digit code, not the password — silently **logged into / auto-created a brand-new empty account**
    (`Vvampirel1988 User`, 0 properties) instead of the real `vampirel1988@gmail.com` test account.
    The old `Set-RentzuFieldValue` only *warned* on a mismatch (and skipped the warning for masked
    fields), so a single blind `input text` immediately after focusing — while the soft keyboard/IME
    is still animating up — was trusted even when it dropped or duplicated a character. This is the
    §0.1 "silent no-op / wrong result" class: the symptom was quiet, so it was easy to proceed past.
    **Fix**: `Set-RentzuFieldValue` now (a) waits longer after focusing before typing, and (b) for
    **readable (non-masked) fields** reads the field back from a fresh dump and, if it doesn't
    exactly equal the requested value, clears it (`KEYCODE_MOVE_END` + backspaces) and retypes — up
    to 3 attempts — then **throws** rather than continue with a wrong value. Masked password fields
    can't be read back, so they keep a best-effort type only. NOTE: since auth was hardened, a
    mistyped **password** is no longer harmless — it now fails with 401 "Invalid email or password"
    at the **Continue with email** step, before any code is sent. A mistyped **email** now creates a
    new account (it registers rather than taking over an existing one), which still silently points
    the test at the wrong, empty account. Never revert this to a
    single blind type + warning. If a login lands on the wrong account, sign out and re-run
    `Invoke-RentzuLogin -ForceReLogin`.

## Cleanup

Screenshots/UI dumps land in `%TEMP%\rentzu-ui-test\` (not the repo), so nothing needs to be
deleted from the repo working tree. If you ever pull them elsewhere for convenience, don't commit
them.
